scores.reasons: Gap: unclaimed profile, no site, no hours, no booking - nothing for an assistant to read or act on. Ability to pay low: tiny single-room studio, negligible review base and no pricing evidence. Ease very high: claiming a profile and a one-page schedule site. Evidence weak: almost all facts come from a directory, not the business.

caveats: Google Maps was viewed in its limited (non-signed-in) mode, so star ratings are shown but review counts were hidden for all ten listings; directory review counts are noted separately where available.

Several of these are small massage businesses; I confirmed only what is publicly listed. I did not verify NJ massage-establishment licensing or any regulatory status for any business, and nothing here should be read as a compliance judgment.

Scores are relative to this batch, not the industry: gap_size 5 means the business is missing most of the basics an AI agent would need, and should not be confused with a high-value engagement on its own.
data_gaps: Review counts on Google were not visible in the limited Maps view; no sign-in was used.
Blue Dream Spa's Google 'Book' button destination could not be determined without clicking through to a third-party booking flow.
Pardon Me Fitness, ProjectSelf and 360 Bodyworks have no first-party web presence, so services and pricing are inferred from directories only.
Phone-width (390px) checks plus screenshots were done for Diesel Gym, SpaKidz, Dhyana Yoga and Iron Strong Athletics; the other six have no working website to check.
ProjectSelf's Facebook page (facebook.com/theprojectself) was not opened - Facebook typically requires a login wall, so it was skipped.
Instagram/Facebook presences for 360 Bodyworks and Pardon Me Fitness could not be confirmed through search.
No contact, quote or booking forms were submitted anywhere, per the read-only rule.
